messages:
mike_support: Heads-up: ACME opened a P1. After we promoted open-llama-v6b to canary they've started getting invalid JSON from the streaming /v1/generate structured_output stream. They say it used to be fine on v5.
julia_se: Can you paste the exact request they sent and the raw streamed bytes (not the parsed log)? We need the precise chunk boundaries.
mike_support: They sent this curl (token redacted):

```
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Redwood-Model: open-llama-v6b-canary" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"generate invoice json\",\"structured_output\":true,\"stream\":true}'
```

mike_support: They pasted the concatenated stream text (we asked for raw event but this is what they have):

```
{"invoice": {"id": "inv_123","total": 125.00}
{"meta": {"tokens": 42}}

```

mike_support: Parser fails with "Unexpected end of JSON input" because the first object is missing a closing brace before the meta object starts.
sanjeev_eng: Thanks. Repro rate reported ~30% after canary bumped to 20% traffic. Sounds like the streaming chunker is splitting a single JSON object across chunks and not emitting a delimiter or atomic object boundaries. That would break naive concat-and-parse clients.
julia_se: Short-term mitigations: ask customer to set stream=false for their org, or pin them to open-llama-v5b. Also request their request_id so we can fetch raw proxy logs.
mike_support: Request id they gave: req_0a1b2c3d. ACME insists they can't change their parser quickly; they want a rollback or hotfix for canary.
deploy-bot: model-swap completed: open-llama-v6b-canary promoted to 20% @ 1768123000
lia_sre: I can roll traffic back for specific orgs if we decide to pin. @sanjeev_eng can you confirm root cause before we rollback platform-wide? We should prefer targeted org pin if possible.
sanjeev_eng: I'll reproduce locally against v6b-canary and capture the streamer output with raw byte offsets. If it's a streamer framing change we either ensure the runtime emits complete JSON objects atomically for structured_output or add an explicit framing layer (e.g., length-prefix or newline delimiter). I'll post a minimal failing test and a patch ETA.
mike_support: ACME wants immediate rollback for their org. Lia, ping me when you can pin org org_acme_42 to v5 so they stop seeing failures.
julia_se: Also filing an incident if we confirm regression. Include failing chunk sequence, request_id, and a unit test to lock behavior.
sanjeev_eng: Reproduced locally: the streamer may emit `"}\n{\"meta\"` across chunks when the KV cache flush happens. Investigating where chunk boundaries are computed in the runtime.
mike_support: Noted. I've sent the workaround (pin to v5 or set stream=false) to ACME and marked P1. Will update when they send raw req_0a1b2c3d logs.
julia_se: Thanks everyone. Once we have the raw proxy trace we can decide fix vs pin. If we need a hotfix, engineering will prioritize given customer impact.
